title: Grateful Dead Live at Omaha Civic Auditorium on 1973-10-21

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1973 fall show with Keith’s stellar keys and a solid soundboard capture despite occasional tape hiss.
ai_review.review: The performance shines with Keith’s exceptional piano work, tight drumming and memorable moments on songs like Here Comes Sunshine, El Paso and the Weather Report Suite > Let It Grow.  The sound‑board source is generally clear but suffers from some tape hiss, a splice on Wharf Rat and occasional static glitches.  Overall listeners rave about the band’s chemistry and energy, rating the show as one of the stronger fall ’73 dates.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the musical performance; recording issues are noted but do not dominate, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear soundboard mix with occasional tape hiss, static, and a splice on Wharf Rat; some reviewers note the recording isn’t totally crystal‑clear but remains listenable.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite > Let It Grow
Playing In The Band > Half-Step > Big River
poor_songs: Here Comes Sunshine (poor sound quality in this version)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is a bit uneven with some sound‑quality hiccups, but the band builds momentum; second set flows stronger with seamless transitions and high‑energy jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pleasant lead vocals and sweet guitar work noted throughout, especially on El Paso and in the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Provides a solid bass foundation; praised for laying down "base bones" early and delivering a huge, deep‑sounding bass in later jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Steady rhythm guitar strumming and vocal contributions are mentioned as keeping the band grounded.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/keyboard playing is highlighted as exceptional throughout the show, with standout moments on El Paso and the Weather Report Suite, though occasional piano noise is noted.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is described as jazzy, high in the mix, and "insane" on Black Throated Wind, driving the overall energy of the performance.
